# Bible Animations

> Free, interactive 3D animated tours of places and events in the Bible, at https://bibletours3d.org/. Each tour flies a camera through a 3D model that is built up step by step in the order the biblical text describes it, stopping to quote the passage, read it aloud and explain what is shown. Only what the text records is modelled; guesses are flagged in the notes.

- Languages: English, Spanish and French (add `?lang=es` or `?lang=fr` to any URL).
- Bible versions: English NASB 2020 (default), NIV, ESV, KJV; Spanish NBLA (default), NVI, RVR1960, RVA 1909; French SG21 (default), BDS, NEG1979, LSG 1910. Pick one with `?version=` (e.g. `?version=kjv`).
- Runs in the browser with WebGL (three.js); no sign-up, no ads. Controls: play/pause, previous/next stop, Explore mode to orbit freely, speed, pause length, narration voice and volume.
- Suitable for Bible study, Sunday school, sermons and classroom teaching.

## Tours

- [Nehemiah’s Wall](https://bibletours3d.org/nehemiahs-wall/) (Nehemiah 3): This is a fly-by of Jerusalem's walls being rebuilt, c. 445 BC. (Inspired by the original fly-by created by Luke Thomas.) The tour goes counter-clockwise from the Sheep Gate, in the same order as Nehemiah 3. The wall starts as ruins: low courses, rubble, and burned gates. Each stretch rises block by block as the camera flies along it. At each of the 25 stops a short popup gives the Bible text, a note, and who did the repairs. A small crew of figures works each stretch, larger where more groups are named; priests are in white.
- [The Dedication of the Wall](https://bibletours3d.org/dedication-of-the-wall/) (Nehemiah 12:27–43): This is a tour of the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, following Nehemiah 12:27–43. The Levites and singers come in from their villages and gather inside the Valley Gate; the priests and Levites purify the people, the gates and the wall; the leaders go up on the wall and two choirs are formed. The first choir, led by Ezra, goes right (south) past the Dung Gate and the Fountain Gate, up the City of David to the Water Gate. The second, with Nehemiah and half the people behind it, goes left (north) past the Tower of Furnaces, the Broad Wall, the Gate of Ephraim, the Old Gate and the Fish Gate, the towers of Hananel and the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate, and stops at the Gate of the Guard. Both choirs then stand in the temple court, and the great sacrifices are offered. The finale is 12:43, "the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away", seen from the Mount of Olives. There are 11 stops.
- [The Tabernacle](https://bibletours3d.org/tabernacle/) (Exodus 25–40): This is a tour of the tabernacle being set up at Sinai, following Exodus 40:17–33. The site starts empty. At each of the 13 stops the next part goes up, in the order Moses set it up: the bases, the boards and bars, the linen curtains, the tent and its coverings, then the furniture from the ark outwards, and the court last. The finale brings the cloud down over the tent, and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle (40:34–38). The popup gives the Bible text, a note, the materials the text names, the size, and who made it.
- [The Priestly Garments](https://bibletours3d.org/priestly-garments/) (Exodus 28 · Leviticus 8:6–9): This is a close-up of Aaron being dressed as high priest at the doorway of the tent of meeting, following Leviticus 8:6–9. Exodus 28 describes the garments and Exodus 39 tells how they were made. At each of the 9 stops Moses puts the next garment on, in the order Leviticus gives: the washing, the tunic, the sash, the robe, the ephod with its shoulder stones and band, the breastpiece, the Urim and Thummim, the turban, and the gold plate. The finale draws back while his four sons are dressed in tunics, sashes and caps (8:13). The popup gives the Bible text, a note, the materials the text names, the size where it is given, and who made it; at the breastpiece it also lists the twelve stones in the current version's names.
- [The Day of Atonement](https://bibletours3d.org/day-of-atonement/) (Leviticus 16): This is a tour of the Day of Atonement at the tabernacle, following Leviticus 16 in its own order. At each of the 15 stops the next step of the rite happens: Aaron bathes and puts on the linen garments; the bull, the two rams and the two goats are brought in; lots are cast over the goats; the bull is slaughtered; Aaron takes coals from the altar and brings incense inside the veil; he sprinkles the bull's blood, then the goat's, on and in front of the cover; he puts blood on the horns of the altar and sprinkles it; he lays his hands on the live goat, which a man leads out through the camp into the wilderness; he leaves the linen garments in the tent and puts on his own; he offers the burnt offerings; and the sin offerings are burned outside the camp. The finale is 16:30, "once a year" (16:34).
- [Holy Week in Jerusalem](https://bibletours3d.org/holy-week/) (Mark 11–16): This is a tour of Jesus' last week in Jerusalem, day by day in Mark's order (Mark 11–16), with the other Gospels where they add to it: the colt at Bethphage, the ride down the Mount of Olives, the weeping over the city (Luke), into the temple; the fig tree and the overturned tables (Monday); Caesar's coin, the widow's two coins and "not one stone upon another" (Tuesday); the anointing at Bethany (Wednesday); the man with the jar of water, the Last Supper and Gethsemane (Thursday); the arrest, Peter's denial, Pilate, Simon of Cyrene, the cross and the burial (Friday); the guard at the tomb (Saturday, from Matthew); and the empty tomb on the first day of the week. The finale is 1 Corinthians 15:3–4, over the city at sunrise. There are 21 stops.
- [Solomon’s Temple](https://bibletours3d.org/solomons-temple/) (1 Kings 6–7 · 2 Chronicles 3–4): This is a tour of Solomon's temple being built on Mount Moriah, in the order of 1 Kings 6–7, with what 2 Chronicles 3–4 adds. The hilltop starts bare. At each of the 21 stops the next part goes up: the foundation, the stone house course by course, the porch, the windows, the side chambers and their winding stair, the cedar roof; then inside, the cedar lining, the inner sanctuary, the gold overlay, the cherubim, the carvings and the doors; the inner court and the great court; and Hiram's bronze work (Jachin and Boaz, the Sea, the ten stands and basins, the bronze altar), the gold furnishings, and the house finished in seven years. The finale is God's word to Solomon in 1 Kings 6:13, circling the finished temple. A few builders and priests stand still to show the scale; the story of the dedication (1 Kings 8) isn't told.
- [Ezekiel’s Temple](https://bibletours3d.org/ezekiels-temple/) (Ezekiel 40–43): This is a tour of the temple Ezekiel saw in his vision (Ezekiel 40–42), on "a very high mountain" (40:2). The man "whose appearance was like bronze" leads Ezekiel round with his measuring rod, and each part goes up as he measures it. The 21 stops go: the man, the outer wall, the three outer gates, the outer court with its pavement and thirty chambers, the inner gates, the tables for the burnt offering, the priests' chambers, the inner court and the altar; then the house, from the porch and its columns to the nave, the most holy place, the side chambers, the building to the west, the house's hundred cubits, the carvings and the wooden altar, and the doors; then the holy chambers, and the wall measured all round. The finale is 43:1–5: the glory of the LORD comes in from the east by the east gate and fills the house; Ezekiel falls on his face and is lifted into the inner court.
- [Paul’s First Missionary Journey](https://bibletours3d.org/pauls-first-journey/) (Acts 13–14): This is a fly-over of Paul and Barnabas's first journey on a map of the real land and sea, with no people shown: the route is drawn as it is travelled, and a ship carries it on the sea crossings. The 18 stops go: Antioch, where the church sends them off (13:3); down to Seleucia; by sea to Salamis; across Cyprus to Paphos, where the proconsul believes; by sea to Perga, where John Mark leaves; over the Taurus Mountains (2 Corinthians 11:26); Pisidian Antioch, the synagogue and "a light for the Gentiles"; Iconium; Lystra, where the crowd takes Barnabas and Paul for Zeus and Hermes, and Paul is stoned; Derbe; back through Lystra and Iconium strengthening the disciples; elders appointed in every church; the churches of Galatia (Galatians 4:13); Perga and Attalia; and by sea home to Antioch. Each stop gives the distance travelled, about 2,100 km in all. The finale is 14:27, "a door of faith to the Gentiles", over the whole route.
- [Paul’s Second Missionary Journey](https://bibletours3d.org/pauls-second-journey/) (Acts 15:36–18:22): A fly-over of Paul's second journey with Silas and Timothy, on the same kind of real map, with no people shown and a ship on the sea crossings. The 18 stops go: Paul chooses Silas at Antioch; through Syria and Cilicia; Timothy at Lystra; the churches strengthened; forbidden to speak in Asia; not into Bithynia; the man of Macedonia at Troas; by Samothrace to Neapolis; Lydia and the jailer at Philippi; Thessalonica; Berea; Athens and the altar "to an unknown god"; Corinth; Cenchrea; Ephesus; and by Caesarea and Jerusalem home to Antioch. The finale is 1 Thessalonians 1:8.
- [Paul’s Third Missionary Journey](https://bibletours3d.org/pauls-third-journey/) (Acts 18:23–21:17): A fly-over of Paul's third journey, on the same kind of real map. The 18 stops go: from Antioch through Galatia and Phrygia (the collection, 1 Corinthians 16:1); Ephesus, "all Asia heard", and the riot in the theater; Troas (2 Corinthians 2:12); Titus in Macedonia (2 Corinthians 7:6); three months in Greece and the gift for the poor in Jerusalem (Romans 15:26); back through Macedonia; breaking bread at Troas; on foot to Assos; by Chios and Samos to Miletus and the farewell to the Ephesian elders; Cos, Rhodes and Patara; past Cyprus to Tyre; Agabus at Caesarea; and Jerusalem. The intro is Acts 20:24 and the finale 21:19.
- [Paul’s Voyage to Rome](https://bibletours3d.org/pauls-voyage-to-rome/) (Acts 27–28): A fly-over of Paul's voyage to Rome as a prisoner, on a real map from Caesarea to Rome, with no people shown and the ship carrying the route; the storm brings dark skies, rain and a rough sea, and the ship is shown aground at Malta. The 18 stops go: bound for Italy at Caesarea; Sidon; in the lee of Cyprus; the Alexandrian ship at Myra; off Cnidus; Fair Havens and Paul's warning; the northeaster (Euraquilo); Cauda; all hope abandoned; the angel's message; the fourteenth night; the shipwreck; Malta; Syracuse; Rhegium and Puteoli; the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns; and Rome. The intro is Acts 23:11 and the finale 28:31, "unhindered".

## Optional

- [Source code and modelling notes](https://github.com/andyrabel/bibleanimations): the README documents each animation’s content decisions and sources.
